question: Is the actual eliminated strong causal response norm-continuous on the high real-frequency ray, and does the fixed-phase auxiliary resonance theorem apply?

primary_sources.title: Hansen and Pedersen, Jensen's Operator Inequality
primary_sources.use: The concave contractive inequality for log(1+x), applied to the multiplier transport after both its ordinary and graph norms are controlled. The unbounded form application is justified by resolvent compression in the note.

primary_sources.title: Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, second edition
primary_sources.use: Bounded-form representation of a resolvent. The common-domain and Lipschitz bounds for the charged shape forms are proved separately, before applying the inverse identity.

comparison: The predecessor constructed separate closed shape realizations and a uniform strong feedback bound at every high real frequency. It did not identify their form domains or prove parameter continuity. The new logarithmic multiplier transport and localized form-derivative estimate supply a common energy space; a positive third-divided-difference argument controls the actual canonical error in graph norm.
hardest_steps: Lift B H_s^-1 from an ordinary graph bound to a logarithmic form-domain bound, without assuming that B commutes with H_s.
Differentiate the compensated logarithmic form using separate outer and interior estimates; the full uncompensated logarithmic norm is not controlled by the outer energy.
Retain all local-action and conformal-reconstruction terms while proving the common form domain, then compose the actual strong feedback in a fixed space.
next_decision: Resolve whether the resulting auxiliary modes or the zero-fast compatible source domain meet the original physical boundary/action, constraint and initial/state requirements, then transfer any conclusion to an actual nonlinear geometry.
